newsitem.title: NETHERLANDS: DUTCH PTT LOOSENS TIES TO CABLE UNIT.
newsitem.headline: DUTCH PTT LOOSENS TIES TO CABLE UNIT.

text.p: Dutch post and telecoms group Koninklijke PTT Nederland NV said on Tuesday it planned to grant management and operational independence to its wholly-owned European cable television infrastructure unit KPN Kabel BV.

The move is a response to a Dutch government demand that PTT Nederland distance itself from NV Casema -- a Dutch cable TV infrastructure firm 77 percent-owned by KPN Kabel -- to make Casema eligible for regional telephony infrastructure licences.
PTT Nederland said it would retain 100 percent ownership for the time being but that KPN Kabel would be converted into an independently managed company to be called Vision Networks NV.
The parent company will no longer consolidate Vision Networks' results in its own figures, though PTT Nederland's profits will include any dividends paid by Vision Networks.
PTT Nederland said the changes would not affect existing plans for KPN Kabel/Vision Networks to enter into partnerships or perhaps to be partially floated on the stock exchange.
A spokesman said the company believed that the planned changes would satisfy the government's demand for looser links between PTT Nederland and Casema.
PTT Nederland currently operates the Netherlands' only national fixed-line telephone system but the government plans to grant licences for one or two competing networks by year end.

Casema is a member of the Enertel consortium of utilities and cable companies which is bidding for one of the national licences but is also interested in using its local cable television networks to offer local telephone services.
